facts.label: Leverage and coverage
facts.text: On the unadjusted measure the ratio fell to 4.94x, but that fall comes from other income of USD 434.5 million in the last twelve months, mainly non-cash gains on the conversion options in the exchangeable notes and on the remeasurement of euro debt. Those gains reverse when the share price or the exchange rate moves back, so they do not service debt, and creditors should anchor on the adjusted ratio. The strongest evidence against this view is that adjusted EBITDA now covers interest expense, net 3.59x over the last twelve months, up from 2.81x in FY2025; but FY2025 carried a USD 202.5 million loss on extinguishment of debt that is not repeated, and the October 2026 notes pay a higher coupon than the 2028 notes they replaced, so the view would change only if adjusted EBITDA recovers or debt falls. facts.label: Cash flow quality
facts.text: Operating cash flow of USD 2,169.0 million over the last twelve months did not cover capital additions of USD 2,729.7 million, leaving a free cash flow deficit of USD 560.7 million, against a deficit of USD 1,182.3 million in FY2025 and a surplus of USD 841.1 million in FY2024. The deficit is the newbuild programme: the delivery of Norwegian Luna in March 2026 and of Norwegian Aqua and Oceania Allura in 2025 were funded mainly by newbuild loans backed by export-credit financing and by revolver borrowings, so debt rises with the fleet and creditors carry delivery and financing-execution risk rather than relying on internally generated cash. The sources split capital spending into maintenance and growth only in guidance for the parent group, so that split is not established for the issuer. facts.label: Liquidity and maturities
facts.text: Liquidity, measured as cash plus revolver availability, fell from USD 1,604.0 million at 31 December 2025 to USD 1,350.7 million at 30 September 2026, and is close to the USD 1,344.3 million of principal scheduled through the end of 2027, which includes the 2027 exchangeable notes that the issuer expects to repay in cash or refinance. limitations: Produced in a host session and accepted by the CP-OS check.
Literal checked analytical handoff, not native contract acceptance; source qualifications and gaps remain.

- Issuer-level pro forma net debt, net leverage and liquidity after the October 2026 refinancing are not established: the quarterly report states the notes issued, the revolver repayment and the export-credit prepayment, but not the principal of the redeemed 2028 notes, the premiums, fees and accrued interest paid or the cash used, and the group release gives pro forma liquidity for the group only. Severity: High. It restricts every statement about post-quarter leverage and liquidity to the 30 September 2026 position. Action: obtain an issuer pro forma statement or the October 2026 current report. - Cash interest paid is not stated for any 2026 period or for the nine months of 2025, so EBITDA over cash interest is not calculable at 31 March, 30 June and 30 September 2026. Severity: Medium. It restricts coverage on cash interest to FY2024 and FY2025, with a proxy on interest expense, net for the interim dates. Action: obtain interest paid for the interim periods. - The FY2025 and FY2024 cash interest amounts include early redemption premiums according to the annual report, and the note does not say how much of each premium is included. Severity: Medium. It restricts recurring cover on cash interest, which is better than the stated 2.81x for FY2025 by an amount that is not established. Action: obtain the split of interest paid between coupon and premium. - The 30 September 2026 quarterly report has no instrument-by-instrument debt table, so the debt instrument register is at 31 December 2025, and the 2026 drawdowns are known only as the Norwegian Luna loan, the 2031 notes issued after the quarter and the exchangeable notes table. Severity: Medium. It restricts debt by instrument, rate and maturity to the year-end position. Action: obtain an instrument-level debt schedule at 30 September 2026. - The revolver drawn balance and any letters of credit at 30 September 2026 are not stated, although the commitment of about USD 2.5 billion and availability of USD 1.1 billion are; availability at 31 December 2024 is not stated, and availability at later dates is stated only to USD 0.1 billion. Severity: Medium. It restricts the precision of liquidity and of undrawn committed facilities. Action: obtain the revolver drawn balance and letters of credit. - The legal rank and security of the export-credit newbuild loans and the exchangeable notes are not stated, so no ranked debt stack or cumulative leverage is drawn. Severity: Medium. It restricts any statement of priority of claims. Action: obtain the debt agreements or an issuer capital structure schedule. - The reconciling items from principal to carrying value include a residual of issuance costs and discounts on the remaining debt that the quarterly report does not itemise; the residual is shown in the calculations after the exchangeable notes discount and the conversion option liabilities. Severity: Medium. It restricts the explanation of the difference between principal and carrying value. Action: obtain the unamortised issuance costs by instrument. - Instrument currency, rate type, spread, floor and scheduled amortisation are not stated for most instruments in the debt table. Severity: Low. It restricts rate and currency exposure by instrument. Action: obtain the debt agreements. - Where the statements print a dash, the cell shows that no figure is supplied and the dash is read as nil only inside sums, for example the current portion of exchangeable notes at 31 December 2025 and the preference shares. Severity: Low. It restricts nothing beyond the label; sums treat the line as nil. Action: none needed. - The annual report states EBITDA for 2025 and 2024 only, so FY2023 EBITDA is calculated by the issuer formula, and FY2023 Adjusted EBITDA and the FY2023 balance sheet are not supplied. Severity: Low. It restricts the FY2023 column of the statements. Action: none needed for the current period. - The balance sheets at 31 March 2025, 30 June 2025 and 30 September 2025 are not in the sources, so leverage cannot be shown at those dates and the prior-year comparison is limited to year-ends. Severity: Low. It restricts year-on-year comparison of interim leverage. Action: obtain the 2025 quarterly balance sheets. - The issuer reports a single segment, so no segment revenue is disclosed and no segment sum is stated. Severity: Low. It restricts brand-level analysis of revenue. Action: obtain brand-level revenue from management. - The statements do not split capital additions into maintenance and growth for the issuer; forward capital spending is split only in group guidance. Severity: Low. It restricts maintenance-capex-adjusted cash flow measures. Action: obtain the maintenance and growth split. - The 2026 statements are unaudited, and last-twelve-months figures combine the audited year with unaudited stubs. Severity: Low. It restricts the evidence grade of the interim ratios. Action: none needed.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Parent control is complete and has so far helped creditors rather than hurt them. Norwegian Cruise Line Holdings Ltd. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against a benign reading is the revolver. The annual report says its maturity becomes 17 November 2026 if the 2027 exchangeable notes, USD 216,175 thousand at 30 September 2026, have not been repaid or refinanced beyond April 2030 and a liquidity test is not met; the amendment of 15 October 2026 may have changed this, but its text is not supplied, and the quarterly report says only that the issuer expects to repay the notes in cash or refinance them before maturity in February 2027. If the trigger survived and the test failed, a facility with about USD 2.8 billion of commitments after the October 2026 amendment, secured on vessels, would fall due 12 days after the as-of date. A second challenge is that a new chief executive, a recent activist agreement and the Havana Docks case against the parent, in which the Supreme Court on 21 May 2026 reversed the dismissal of a claim that had produced a judgment of USD 112.9 million, could push parent policy toward shareholder returns or asset sales. Governance risk would move to Low on the amendment text removing the trigger and holding distribution limits, and to High on any cash distribution to the parent, a release of collateral without repayment, or cash settlement of exchangeable notes while the parent issues shares to others. facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: In October 2026 NCL Corporation Ltd. issued USD 950.0 million of senior unsecured notes due 15 October 2031 under an indenture dated 15 October 2026. The notes pay 8.75% a year, are redeemable at a make-whole price before 15 October 2028 and allow up to 40% to be redeemed from equity proceeds at 108.75% of principal. The proceeds and cash on hand redeemed all of the 6.125% senior notes due 2028, repaid USD 380.0 million of revolver borrowings and prepaid about USD 42.2 million of export-credit loans, together with accrued interest and any premiums, fees and expenses, none of which is stated. On the same date the third amendment to the revolving credit agreement raised commitments from about USD 2.5 billion to about USD 2.8 billion and modified financial covenant definitions and collateral; neither the amended terms nor the collateral changes are described. The 30 September 2026 balance sheet is not pro forma for these events, and issuer-level pro forma net debt, leverage and liquidity are not stated. The new notes pay a coupon 2.625 percentage points above the 6.125% notes redeemed, and the identified uses of USD 947.2 million are close to the USD 950.0 million raised on the assumption that the original USD 525.0 million of 2028 notes was still outstanding. facts.text: In 2025 the issuer refinanced most of its unsecured and secured notes. In April 2025 it exchanged USD 353.9 million of 2025 exchangeable notes for 2030 notes and a cash payment of about USD 64.0 million funded by a parent share sale, and in June 2025 it raised revolver commitments to about USD 2.5 billion. In September 2025 it issued about USD 1.4 billion of 2030 exchangeable notes, USD 1.2 billion of 5.875% notes due 2031 and USD 850.0 million of 6.25% notes due 2033, repurchased USD 958.0 million and USD 449.0 million of 2027 exchangeable notes for about USD 1,009.5 million and USD 480.5 million, repaid the 2026, 2027 and 2029 notes, and secured the revolver on nine vessels. FY2025 interest expense includes about USD 202.5 million of losses on extinguishment and modification of debt.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Leverage is high and has not fallen, and reported EBITDA flatters it. Total debt was 5.51x last-twelve-months adjusted EBITDA at 30 September 2026, against 5.34x at 31 December 2025 and 5.43x at 31 December 2024, and net debt was 5.42x. On reported EBITDA the ratio is 4.94x, but that measure includes USD 434.5 million of other income over the period, mostly non-cash gains on the conversion options in the exchangeable notes and on euro debt, so adjusted EBITDA is the safer yardstick. Balance-sheet debt grew by USD 301,032 thousand in nine months while adjusted EBITDA slipped, so deleveraging is not yet visible; the net debt and leverage after the 15 October 2026 notes issue, redemption and revolver repayment are not established. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 23; calculation A1; calculation L1; calculation L2; calculation L3; calculation D2

facts.text: Free cash flow is negative and capital spending is largely committed, so debt keeps rising with the fleet. Operating cash flow of USD 2,169.0 million over the last twelve months did not cover additions to property and equipment of USD 2,729.7 million, a deficit of USD 560.7 million, after a deficit of USD 1,182.3 million in FY2025. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Liquidity covers the next maturities only about once, and the 2030 maturities are the refinancing test. Cash plus revolver availability of USD 1,350.7 million at 30 September 2026 is 1.00x the USD 1,344.3 million of principal due by the end of 2027, and USD 4,134.3 million, or 26.68% of scheduled principal, falls due in 2030 when the revolver and the 2030 exchangeable notes mature. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against a cautious view is that the business is beating its own guidance and funding is committed. The parent reports third-quarter adjusted EBITDA of USD 937 million against guidance of USD 874 million, expects 2027 Net Yield growth, and has announced savings of USD 125 million plus about USD 100 million twice; the issuer's own unit cost excluding fuel fell 0.66% while yield fell, committed undrawn export-credit facilities of about USD 10.8 billion fund about 80% of effective ship contracts, and the October 2026 financing raised revolver commitments to about USD 2.8 billion. If Net Yield stabilises, savings reach the margin and last-twelve-months leverage falls below the FY2025 level of 5.34x, the profile would move from stretched to adequate. If instead the annual report's revolver trigger survived the October amendment, Net Yield falls further than guided, or leverage rises above 5.51x without refinancing of the 2030 maturities, the view would weaken. On the parent's full-year guidance and debt unchanged from 30 September 2026, total debt would be 5.84x adjusted EBITDA at year-end, so leverage is more likely to rise than fall in 2026 before the 2027 recovery that management expects, and the October 2026 financing effect on debt is not established. Over three to five years deliveries continue to 2037, with non-cancelable payments of USD 3,274,155 thousand in 2030 alone, so deleveraging depends on earnings growth from new capacity, not on lower spending. facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: The initiating condition is a further fall in Caribbean pricing as new capacity arrives and the Middle East conflict keeps Europe and Asia-Pacific demand weak. The first operational break is the booking curve, which management already describes as below its optimal range, so ships sail full at lower prices; at the parent's stated sensitivity a further 5% fall in Net Yield removes about USD 380 million of adjusted EBITDA, taking last-twelve-months adjusted EBITDA to USD 2,320.1 million, leverage to 6.42x, interest cover to 3.08x and free cash flow to a deficit of USD 940.7 million. The financing consequence is that liquidity of USD 1,350.7 million, about equal to principal due through 2027, would be drawn to fund the gap while export-credit financing still covers about 80% of ship contracts, and the 2030 maturities of USD 4,134.3 million would have to be refinanced at leverage of 6.42x. Management levers are the savings programmes, the sale or charter of older ships and the reset of delivery dates; the parent has contributed equity before but is not committed to do so. The observable triggers are adjusted EBITDA below guidance, a fourth-quarter Net Yield decline worse than the guided 6.5%, and any sign that the contingent revolver maturity applies. Management states that liquidity is sufficient for at least the next 12 months, and in the stress case resilience rests on export-credit draws and the revolver rather than on internally generated cash, so it is enough to avoid distress but not to deleverage. facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, NCL Corporation presents an adequate business profile supported by scale across three brands, prepaid bookings and demonstrated market access, but credit quality is constrained by leverage of 5.51x adjusted EBITDA, negative free cash flow and falling yields. Cash-flow durability appears weak to adequate because earnings are price-sensitive while ship payments are fixed. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on stabilising Net Yield, the unverified revolver terms and the 2030 maturities. The primary downside path is yield erosion on growing capacity that raises leverage and widens the funding gap before 2030. Further analysis would require the credit agreement and amendment, an issuer-level pro forma position after October 2026, interim cash interest and peer or market evidence. Top risk: yield erosion. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0); calculation L1; calculation S1

## Findings
### Bottom line

The supplied filings are sufficient for Financial foundation, Business & governance and Fundamental credit work on the issuer's own statements, but without the credit agreement and indentures covenant protection cannot be tested, and the October 2026 refinancing postdates the latest balance sheet.

The issuer is a wholly owned subsidiary of Norwegian Cruise Line Holdings, so its own annual and quarterly reports must carry every debt, earnings and liquidity figure. The three results releases describe the parent group and differ from the issuer on net income, cash and debt. The October 2026 refinancing is described in amounts only, so issuer-level pro forma debt and leverage are not established. The annual report gives levels for three covenant tests but none for the net funded debt to capitalization test, and the amendment that changed the covenant definitions is not supplied.

## Request

Financial foundation for NCL CORP Ltd. as of 2026-11-05 on the credit_snapshot pathway. The scope is the issuer's own statements for FY2023 to FY2025 and the 2026 quarters, with net debt, leverage, coverage, liquidity, maturities and events after the latest balance sheet; the parent group's results releases are context only.

## Findings
### Bottom line

NCL Corporation's total debt stood at 5.51x last-twelve-months adjusted EBITDA at 30 September 2026, up from 5.34x at year-end, and free cash flow is negative, so creditors rely on export-credit funding and revolver access.
Basis: calculation L1; calculation L2; calculation F1

Reported EBITDA gives a lower 4.94x because it includes non-cash gains, so the adjusted measure is the safer yardstick. Cover of EBITDA over cash interest was 2.81x in FY2025, and no cash interest is stated for 2026. Liquidity of USD 1,350.7 million at 30 September 2026 is close to the USD 1,344.3 million of principal due by the end of 2027. The October 2026 refinancing is not in these figures, and its effect on net debt is not established.
Basis: calculation L3; calculation C1; calculation Q1; calculation Q2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 38
### Leverage and coverage

Adjusted leverage rose during 2026 while the unadjusted figure fell. Total debt was 5.51x last-twelve-months adjusted EBITDA at 30 September 2026, against 5.34x at 31 December 2025 and 5.43x at 31 December 2024: debt at carrying value grew from USD 14,583.4 million to USD 14,884.5 million while adjusted EBITDA slipped from USD 2,731.4 million to USD 2,700.1 million, because the nine months to September 2026 earned less adjusted EBITDA than the same months of 2025. The effect for creditors is that deleveraging is not yet visible in the issuer's own statements.
Basis: calculation D2; calculation D5; calculation A3; calculation L1; calculation L2

On the unadjusted measure the ratio fell to 4.94x, but that fall comes from other income of USD 434.5 million in the last twelve months, mainly non-cash gains on the conversion options in the exchangeable notes and on the remeasurement of euro debt. Those gains reverse when the share price or the exchange rate moves back, so they do not service debt, and creditors should anchor on the adjusted ratio. The strongest evidence against this view is that adjusted EBITDA now covers interest expense, net 3.59x over the last twelve months, up from 2.81x in FY2025; but FY2025 carried a USD 202.5 million loss on extinguishment of debt that is not repeated, and the October 2026 notes pay a higher coupon than the 2028 notes they replaced, so the view would change only if adjusted EBITDA recovers or debt falls.

Basis: calculation L3; calculation E3; calculation A3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-12-31_nclc-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 150

Cover on cash interest was 2.81x in FY2025 and 3.06x in FY2024. The annual report says those cash interest amounts include early redemption premiums, so recurring cover is better than stated, and no cash interest is stated for any 2026 period, so last-twelve-months cover on cash interest is not calculable. Interest expense, net for FY2025 includes a loss on extinguishment of debt, which is why the proxy cover was 2.81x for FY2025 against 3.59x for the last twelve months.
Basis: calculation C1; 10-K_2025-12-31_nclc-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 169; 10-K_2025-12-31_nclc-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 121
### Cash flow quality

Operating cash flow of USD 2,169.0 million over the last twelve months did not cover capital additions of USD 2,729.7 million, leaving a free cash flow deficit of USD 560.7 million, against a deficit of USD 1,182.3 million in FY2025 and a surplus of USD 841.1 million in FY2024. The deficit is the newbuild programme: the delivery of Norwegian Luna in March 2026 and of Norwegian Aqua and Oceania Allura in 2025 were funded mainly by newbuild loans backed by export-credit financing and by revolver borrowings, so debt rises with the fleet and creditors carry delivery and financing-execution risk rather than relying on internally generated cash. The sources split capital spending into maintenance and growth only in guidance for the parent group, so that split is not established for the issuer.
Basis: calculation F1; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 40; 10-K_2025-12-31_nclc-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 123
### Liquidity and maturities

Liquidity, measured as cash plus revolver availability, fell from USD 1,604.0 million at 31 December 2025 to USD 1,350.7 million at 30 September 2026, and is close to the USD 1,344.3 million of principal scheduled through the end of 2027, which includes the 2027 exchangeable notes that the issuer expects to repay in cash or refinance. The largest scheduled amount falls in 2030, when the revolver and the 2030 exchangeable notes mature. The October 2026 refinancing replaced the 2028 notes with notes due 2031, repaid part of the revolver and raised revolver commitments, which the group release puts at USD 2.1 billion of pro forma liquidity for the group; the issuer's own pro forma figures are not established, and export-credit facilities that fund ships are excluded from liquidity.

Basis: calculation Q1; calculation Q2; calculation M1; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 38; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_exh_991.htm.jsonl, page 3
### Customer deposits and subsequent events

Customer deposits held as advance ticket sales were USD 3,142.0 million at 30 September 2026, against USD 3,200.6 million at 31 December 2025 and USD 3,106.0 million at 31 December 2024, and they are many times cash of USD 250.7 million. This float funds operations without interest, so a fall in bookings, or a card-processor reserve requirement (none was required at 30 September 2026), would drain cash quickly; it is working-capital funding, not payables. Events after 30 September 2026 are kept out of the period figures: the October 2026 notes issue, redemption of the 2028 notes, revolver and export-credit repayments and the revolver amendment, and the sale agreement for Oceania Insignia with closing in September 2027.
### Data quality and definitions

The issuer reports one segment, so no segment revenue is available. Statements for the 2026 periods are unaudited, FY2025 is audited with an unqualified opinion, and last-twelve-months figures combine an audited year with unaudited stubs. Debt is carried at balance-sheet value including conversion option liabilities, so it is below the principal in the repayment schedule; the results releases describe the parent group and differ from the issuer on net income, debt and cash, so they are not used for issuer figures.

## Gaps

- Issuer-level pro forma net debt, net leverage and liquidity after the October 2026 refinancing are not established: the quarterly report states the notes issued, the revolver repayment and the export-credit prepayment, but not the principal of the redeemed 2028 notes, the premiums, fees and accrued interest paid or the cash used, and the group release gives pro forma liquidity for the group only. Severity: High. It restricts every statement about post-quarter leverage and liquidity to the 30 September 2026 position. Action: obtain an issuer pro forma statement or the October 2026 current report.

- Cash interest paid is not stated for any 2026 period or for the nine months of 2025, so EBITDA over cash interest is not calculable at 31 March, 30 June and 30 September 2026. Severity: Medium. It restricts coverage on cash interest to FY2024 and FY2025, with a proxy on interest expense, net for the interim dates. Action: obtain interest paid for the interim periods.

- The FY2025 and FY2024 cash interest amounts include early redemption premiums according to the annual report, and the note does not say how much of each premium is included. Severity: Medium. It restricts recurring cover on cash interest, which is better than the stated 2.81x for FY2025 by an amount that is not established. Action: obtain the split of interest paid between coupon and premium.

- The 30 September 2026 quarterly report has no instrument-by-instrument debt table, so the debt instrument register is at 31 December 2025, and the 2026 drawdowns are known only as the Norwegian Luna loan, the 2031 notes issued after the quarter and the exchangeable notes table. Severity: Medium. It restricts debt by instrument, rate and maturity to the year-end position. Action: obtain an instrument-level debt schedule at 30 September 2026.

- The revolver drawn balance and any letters of credit at 30 September 2026 are not stated, although the commitment of about USD 2.5 billion and availability of USD 1.1 billion are; availability at 31 December 2024 is not stated, and availability at later dates is stated only to USD 0.1 billion. Severity: Medium. It restricts the precision of liquidity and of undrawn committed facilities. Action: obtain the revolver drawn balance and letters of credit.

- The legal rank and security of the export-credit newbuild loans and the exchangeable notes are not stated, so no ranked debt stack or cumulative leverage is drawn. Severity: Medium. It restricts any statement of priority of claims. Action: obtain the debt agreements or an issuer capital structure schedule.

- The reconciling items from principal to carrying value include a residual of issuance costs and discounts on the remaining debt that the quarterly report does not itemise; the residual is shown in the calculations after the exchangeable notes discount and the conversion option liabilities. Severity: Medium. It restricts the explanation of the difference between principal and carrying value. Action: obtain the unamortised issuance costs by instrument.

- Instrument currency, rate type, spread, floor and scheduled amortisation are not stated for most instruments in the debt table. Severity: Low. It restricts rate and currency exposure by instrument. Action: obtain the debt agreements.

- Where the statements print a dash, the cell shows that no figure is supplied and the dash is read as nil only inside sums, for example the current portion of exchangeable notes at 31 December 2025 and the preference shares. Severity: Low. It restricts nothing beyond the label; sums treat the line as nil. Action: none needed.

- The annual report states EBITDA for 2025 and 2024 only, so FY2023 EBITDA is calculated by the issuer formula, and FY2023 Adjusted EBITDA and the FY2023 balance sheet are not supplied. Severity: Low. It restricts the FY2023 column of the statements. Action: none needed for the current period.

- The balance sheets at 31 March 2025, 30 June 2025 and 30 September 2025 are not in the sources, so leverage cannot be shown at those dates and the prior-year comparison is limited to year-ends. Severity: Low. It restricts year-on-year comparison of interim leverage. Action: obtain the 2025 quarterly balance sheets.

- The issuer reports a single segment, so no segment revenue is disclosed and no segment sum is stated. Severity: Low. It restricts brand-level analysis of revenue. Action: obtain brand-level revenue from management.

- The statements do not split capital additions into maintenance and growth for the issuer; forward capital spending is split only in group guidance. Severity: Low. It restricts maintenance-capex-adjusted cash flow measures. Action: obtain the maintenance and growth split.

- The 2026 statements are unaudited, and last-twelve-months figures combine the audited year with unaudited stubs. Severity: Low. It restricts the evidence grade of the interim ratios. Action: none needed.

## Findings
### Bottom line

NCL Corporation is a wholly owned subsidiary that the parent supported with equity in 2025 and has not drained, so governance risk is Medium and creditors' exposure rests on the issuer's own covenants and liquidity rather than on parent behaviour.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_nclc-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-K_2025-12-31_nclc-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, pages 123–124; Source readiness (CP-0); calculation C1

Leadership turnover in 2026, an activist agreement at the parent and a signed transition agreement for the finance chief raise execution risk. The October 2026 refinancing extended maturities at a higher coupon, but its amended covenants cannot be checked, and the annual report's contingent 17 November 2026 maturity for the revolver is not cleared by the quarterly report.
### Key findings

Parent control is complete and has so far helped creditors rather than hurt them. Norwegian Cruise Line Holdings Ltd. (NCLH) owns 100% of the ordinary shares, it contributed equity of USD 275,054 thousand in 2025 of which USD 144,980 thousand was cash from its own share sales, and the cash flow statements show no distribution to it in 2023, 2024, 2025 or the first nine months of 2026. The debt agreements restrict distributions to the parent, but their text is not supplied, so the protection is observed behaviour rather than tested capacity.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_nclc-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-K_2025-12-31_nclc-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-K_2025-12-31_nclc-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 71; 10-K_2025-12-31_nclc-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, pages 123–124; 10-K_2025-12-31_nclc-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 90; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C1; calculation C2

The issuer carries almost all of the group's debt, so its own statements are the credit and the parent's releases are context. At 30 September 2026 the issuer's balance-sheet debt was USD 14,884,473 thousand against USD 15,086,503 thousand for the parent, a gap of USD 202,030 thousand, or 1.34% of the parent figure. The effect of the October 2026 refinancing on net debt and leverage is not established.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_exh_991.htm.jsonl, page 18; calculation C3; calculation C4

The October 2026 refinancing bought time at a higher cost, and its legal terms are not visible. NCL Corporation issued USD 950.0 million of senior unsecured notes due 2031 and used the proceeds with cash on hand to redeem the 2028 notes, repay USD 380.0 million of revolver borrowings and prepay about USD 42.2 million of export-credit loans, while revolver commitments rose from about USD 2.5 billion to about USD 2.8 billion. The new notes carry a higher coupon than the 2028 notes they replace, and the amendment changed covenant definitions and collateral in terms the filings do not give, so covenant headroom after it is not established.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 50; 10-K_2025-12-31_nclc-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 140; calculation C5; calculation C6

Leadership, board and shareholder pressure at the parent changed materially in 2026, which raises execution risk during a turnaround. A new chief executive took office in February 2026, the parent signed a cooperation agreement with Elliott entities on 26 March 2026, five independent directors joined the parent board from 31 March 2026, and on 27 October 2026 the finance chief signed a transition agreement while an employment agreement was signed with another executive whose role is not stated. The issuer bore USD 5,392 thousand of advisory fees for activist activity and USD 22,387 thousand of restructuring costs in the nine months to September 2026.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_nclc-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-03-31_nclc-20260331x10q.htm.jsonl, page 42; EX-99.1_2026-05-04_exh_991.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 50; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 35; calculation C8

Commercial execution, not scale, is the weak point of the operating model. In the nine months to September 2026 Capacity Days (berths available multiplied by cruise days) grew 8.69% but Net Yield (adjusted gross margin per Capacity Day) fell 3.42%, so revenue rose only 4.42% and operating income fell 11.18% to USD 1,221,395 thousand; passenger ticket revenue grew 0.78% while onboard and other revenue, which includes ship charter income, grew 12.27%. About 84% of revenue comes from U.S.-sourced guests, and management describes the booked position as below its optimal range.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 34; calculation C9; calculation C10

Newbuild commitments, not shareholder payouts, drive capital allocation, so debt rises with the fleet. Non-cancelable ship construction payments total USD 19,421,174 thousand at 30 September 2026, of which USD 864,295 thousand falls in the rest of 2026, and export-credit financing is expected to fund about 80% of each effective contract, with about USD 10.8 billion of committed undrawn export-credit facilities. Free cash flow after ship additions was a deficit of USD 582,741 thousand in the nine months, and balance-sheet debt is USD 301,032 thousand higher than at 31 December 2025 although no distribution was paid.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-K_2025-12-31_nclc-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 122; calculation C3; calculation C11; calculation C16

Fleet disposals and charters monetise older ships but are not tied to debt reduction in the filings. Oceania Sirena was sold in September 2026 for cash proceeds of USD 104,995 thousand and a loss of USD 16,825 thousand, and is still operated under a bareboat charter to spring 2028; Norwegian Sky, Norwegian Sun and Seven Seas Navigator are chartered or leased, and Oceania Insignia is agreed for sale with closing in September 2027 at a price not stated. The use of the Sirena proceeds is not stated.

The reduced disclosure format limits what creditors can verify about governance. As a wholly owned voluntary filer the issuer omits directors, compensation, ownership and related-party items and incorporates them from the parent's proxy statement, which is not supplied; the audit opinion is unqualified, and the only related-party balance visible is USD 56,145 thousand due to the parent.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_nclc-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 94; 10-K_2025-12-31_nclc-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 118; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 3; Source readiness (CP-0)
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a benign reading is the revolver. The annual report says its maturity becomes 17 November 2026 if the 2027 exchangeable notes, USD 216,175 thousand at 30 September 2026, have not been repaid or refinanced beyond April 2030 and a liquidity test is not met; the amendment of 15 October 2026 may have changed this, but its text is not supplied, and the quarterly report says only that the issuer expects to repay the notes in cash or refinance them before maturity in February 2027. If the trigger survived and the test failed, a facility with about USD 2.8 billion of commitments after the October 2026 amendment, secured on vessels, would fall due 12 days after the as-of date. A second challenge is that a new chief executive, a recent activist agreement and the Havana Docks case against the parent, in which the Supreme Court on 21 May 2026 reversed the dismissal of a claim that had produced a judgment of USD 112.9 million, could push parent policy toward shareholder returns or asset sales. Governance risk would move to Low on the amendment text removing the trigger and holding distribution limits, and to High on any cash distribution to the parent, a release of collateral without repayment, or cash settlement of exchangeable notes while the parent issues shares to others.

### Limitations

- No executed credit agreement, indenture or amendment is supplied, so the filings' statement that debt agreements restrict distributions to the parent cannot be tested for amount or baskets; this keeps the Medium rating a judgement on observed behaviour and leaves the capacity to distribute unmeasured.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_nclc-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 90; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 50; Source readiness (CP-0)

- Directors, compensation and related-party terms sit in the parent's proxy statement, which is not supplied, so the governance rating rests on filings, exhibit titles and parent releases and could move on any fee or related-party arrangement that the proxy shows.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_nclc-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 94; EX-99.1_2026-05-04_exh_991.htm.jsonl, page 1

- The terms of the activist agreement, the names of the new directors and the role of the executive named in the new employment agreement are not supplied, so the effect of activism on financial policy is not established and the leadership-turnover concern is not sized.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-03-31_nclc-20260331x10q.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 50; EX-99.1_2026-05-04_exh_991.htm.jsonl, page 1
- Brand-level revenue is not disclosed because one segment is reported, so concentration across the three brands cannot be tested and the revenue-mix view rests on revenue type and destination only.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_nclc-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 128

- Only USD 144,980 thousand of the 2025 parent contribution is shown as cash; the remaining USD 130,074 thousand is not itemised, so the weight of cash support in the supportive-behaviour conclusion is partly unknown.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_nclc-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, pages 123–124; calculation C1

- The pro forma debt, liquidity and leverage of the issuer after the October 2026 financing are not stated, so any conclusion on the benefit of the refinancing is limited to the amounts, coupon and extension disclosed.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12; Source readiness (CP-0)

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

In October 2026 NCL Corporation Ltd. issued USD 950.0 million of senior unsecured notes due 15 October 2031 under an indenture dated 15 October 2026. The notes pay 8.75% a year, are redeemable at a make-whole price before 15 October 2028 and allow up to 40% to be redeemed from equity proceeds at 108.75% of principal. The proceeds and cash on hand redeemed all of the 6.125% senior notes due 2028, repaid USD 380.0 million of revolver borrowings and prepaid about USD 42.2 million of export-credit loans, together with accrued interest and any premiums, fees and expenses, none of which is stated. On the same date the third amendment to the revolving credit agreement raised commitments from about USD 2.5 billion to about USD 2.8 billion and modified financial covenant definitions and collateral; neither the amended terms nor the collateral changes are described. The 30 September 2026 balance sheet is not pro forma for these events, and issuer-level pro forma net debt, leverage and liquidity are not stated. The new notes pay a coupon 2.625 percentage points above the 6.125% notes redeemed, and the identified uses of USD 947.2 million are close to the USD 950.0 million raised on the assumption that the original USD 525.0 million of 2028 notes was still outstanding.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 50; 10-K_2025-12-31_nclc-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 140; calculation C5; calculation C6

In 2025 the issuer refinanced most of its unsecured and secured notes. In January 2025 it issued USD 1.8 billion of 6.75% senior unsecured notes due 2032 and redeemed USD 1.2 billion of 5.875% notes due 2026 and USD 600.0 million of 8.375% senior secured notes due 2028 while raising the revolver from USD 1.2 billion to USD 1.7 billion with maturity extended to 2030. In April 2025 it exchanged USD 353.9 million of 2025 exchangeable notes for 2030 notes and a cash payment of about USD 64.0 million funded by a parent share sale, and in June 2025 it raised revolver commitments to about USD 2.5 billion. In September 2025 it issued about USD 1.4 billion of 2030 exchangeable notes, USD 1.2 billion of 5.875% notes due 2031 and USD 850.0 million of 6.25% notes due 2033, repurchased USD 958.0 million and USD 449.0 million of 2027 exchangeable notes for about USD 1,009.5 million and USD 480.5 million, repaid the 2026, 2027 and 2029 notes, and secured the revolver on nine vessels. FY2025 interest expense includes about USD 202.5 million of losses on extinguishment and modification of debt.

New ships are financed by export-credit loans of about 80% of each contract price: Norwegian Aqua (March 2025, EUR 1.0 billion at 1.83% to 2037), Oceania Allura (July 2025, EUR 570.4 million at 1.50% to 2037) and Norwegian Luna (March 2026, EUR 1.0 billion at 1.91% to 2038). At 30 September 2026 contract prices for 13 effective newbuilds were about EUR 18.0 billion, or USD 20.4 billion, and Seven Seas Prestige is scheduled for 2026, Norwegian Aura and Oceania Sonata for 2027; the parent's third-quarter release says the Seven Seas Prestige delivery slipped to late December.

The issuer is selling or chartering older ships. Oceania Sirena was sold in September 2026 and continues in service under a bareboat charter to spring 2028; a ten-year bareboat charter of Norwegian Sky began in September 2026 with fixed payments of USD 15.3 million for two years and USD 13.3 million a year afterwards, a similar charter for Norwegian Sun starts in late 2027, a nine-year lease of Seven Seas Navigator starts in December 2027, Oceania Regatta began a two-year time charter in September 2026, and a memorandum of agreement for Oceania Insignia targets closing in September 2027. Oceania Nautica is retained for refurbishment and is expected to be renamed Oceania Aurelia in late 2027.

Exchangeable notes tie the issuer to its parent's shares. At 30 September 2026 USD 192,037 thousand of 1.125% and USD 24,138 thousand of 2.5% exchangeable notes due 15 February 2027 remain outstanding, the issuer irrevocably chose cash settlement in May 2026 and expects to repay them in cash or refinance before maturity; the 2030 exchangeable notes (USD 353,876 thousand and USD 1,407,000 thousand) are guaranteed by the parent and settle principal in cash. The annual report also describes a contingent maturity of the revolver on 17 November 2026 tied to these 2027 notes, which the quarterly report does not restate.

# NCL CORP Ltd. - Fundamental credit as of 2026-11-05
## Request

Fundamental credit assessment of NCL CORP Ltd. as of 2026-11-05 on the credit_snapshot pathway (Full credit assessment). The scope is the issuer's own business and financial profile, refinancing capacity, downside path and monitoring triggers, built on the supplied filings and the Source readiness, Financial foundation and Business & governance analyses. No peer, market, rating-agency, legal-document or portfolio input is supplied, and the parent group's releases are read as context only.

## Findings
### Bottom line

NCL Corporation has an adequate business profile and stretched finances: leverage is 5.51x adjusted EBITDA and not falling, free cash flow is negative while newbuilds are delivered and yields are falling, so creditors depend on refinancing access and export-credit funding rather than deleveraging.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation L1; calculation F1; calculation Y1

Total debt was 5.51x last-twelve-months adjusted EBITDA at 30 September 2026, up from 5.34x at 31 December 2025, and free cash flow was a deficit of USD 560.7 million; pro forma leverage after the 15 October 2026 notes issue is not established. Liquidity of USD 1,350.7 million about equals the USD 1,344.3 million of principal due by the end of 2027, and USD 4,134.3 million falls due in 2030. The primary downside is further yield erosion, which at the parent's stated sensitivity would lift leverage to 6.42x if Net Yield fell a further 5%.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 38; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_exh_991.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation L1; calculation F1; calculation Q1; calculation M1; calculation S1
### Key findings

Leverage is high and has not fallen, and reported EBITDA flatters it. Total debt was 5.51x last-twelve-months adjusted EBITDA at 30 September 2026, against 5.34x at 31 December 2025 and 5.43x at 31 December 2024, and net debt was 5.42x. On reported EBITDA the ratio is 4.94x, but that measure includes USD 434.5 million of other income over the period, mostly non-cash gains on the conversion options in the exchangeable notes and on euro debt, so adjusted EBITDA is the safer yardstick. Balance-sheet debt grew by USD 301,032 thousand in nine months while adjusted EBITDA slipped, so deleveraging is not yet visible; the net debt and leverage after the 15 October 2026 notes issue, redemption and revolver repayment are not established.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 23; calculation A1; calculation L1; calculation L2; calculation L3; calculation D2

Free cash flow is negative and capital spending is largely committed, so debt keeps rising with the fleet. Operating cash flow of USD 2,169.0 million over the last twelve months did not cover additions to property and equipment of USD 2,729.7 million, a deficit of USD 560.7 million, after a deficit of USD 1,182.3 million in FY2025. Non-cancelable ship construction payments total USD 19,421,174 thousand, so spending cannot be cut quickly, and export-credit financing is expected to fund about 80% of each effective contract, with about USD 10.8 billion of committed undrawn facilities. Newbuild and growth spending not covered by export-credit financing in place is about USD 0.5 billion for the rest of 2026 and USD 1.1 billion in 2027.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 40–42; calculation F1; calculation E1

Earnings power is eroding at the margin as capacity growth meets falling yields. Net Yield fell 3.42% in the nine months and 6.51% in the third quarter while Capacity Days grew 8.69%, so revenue rose 4.42% and operating income fell 11.18%; third-quarter adjusted EBITDA fell 8.11% to USD 936.7 million. The parent guides full-year adjusted EBITDA to about USD 2.55 billion, which is 6.64% below FY2025, and management expects Net Yield growth of 1% to 2% in 2027, although the booked position for the first half of 2027 is below last year's.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 36; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_exh_991.htm.jsonl, pages 1–4; calculation Y1; calculation Y2; calculation G1

Liquidity covers the next maturities only about once, and the 2030 maturities are the refinancing test. Cash plus revolver availability of USD 1,350.7 million at 30 September 2026 is 1.00x the USD 1,344.3 million of principal due by the end of 2027, and USD 4,134.3 million, or 26.68% of scheduled principal, falls due in 2030 when the revolver and the 2030 exchangeable notes mature. The October 2026 financing replaced the 2028 notes and raised revolver commitments, which the parent says lifts group liquidity to USD 2.1 billion pro forma, but the issuer-level figure is not established. The revolver's contingent 17 November 2026 maturity is unverified, and its maturity also springs forward if senior notes above USD 400,000,000 are not refinanced 91 days before they fall due, which makes the USD 600.0 million of notes due 2029 a second test.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 38; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_exh_991.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-K_2025-12-31_nclc-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 140; 10-K_2025-12-31_nclc-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 142; calculation Q1; calculation M1; calculation R1

Market access is open but costs more. The issuer raised USD 1.8 billion, USD 1.2 billion and USD 850.0 million of senior notes in 2025 and USD 950.0 million in October 2026, and its latest three newbuild loans carry fixed rates of 1.50% to 1.91%, but the 2031 notes pay a coupon above the 2028 notes they replaced. Interest expense, net excluding extinguishment losses fell only 2.65% in the nine months while debt rose, and adjusted EBITDA covered interest expense, net 3.59x over the last twelve months against 2.81x in FY2025, helped by the absence of last year's extinguishment losses.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_nclc-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 78; 10-K_2025-12-31_nclc-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, pages 142–144; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 35; calculation I1; calculation I2

Demand is concentrated and exposed to fuel, euro and geopolitical shocks. About 84% of revenue comes from U.S.-sourced guests, North America was 63.04% of nine-month revenue against 57.48% in FY2025 while Europe fell 11.80% and Asia-Pacific fell 22.96%, fuel expense rose 14.90% with about 48% hedged for the rest of 2026, and euro ship contracts and euro debt are partly unhedged.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-K_2025-12-31_nclc-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 79; calculation G2; calculation K1

Customer deposits are the main operating cushion and the main liability if sentiment turns. Advance ticket sales were USD 3,141,976 thousand at 30 September 2026, 12.53x cash, about 45% of contract liabilities are refundable, and no card-processor reserve was required.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 23; calculation D1

Governance adds a modest risk rather than a driver of the view. The parent supported the issuer with equity in 2025, no distribution to it appears in the statements, and the debt agreements restrict distributions, but the agreements are not supplied, the chief executive and board changed in 2026 and the finance chief has signed a transition agreement.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a cautious view is that the business is beating its own guidance and funding is committed. The parent reports third-quarter adjusted EBITDA of USD 937 million against guidance of USD 874 million, expects 2027 Net Yield growth, and has announced savings of USD 125 million plus about USD 100 million twice; the issuer's own unit cost excluding fuel fell 0.66% while yield fell, committed undrawn export-credit facilities of about USD 10.8 billion fund about 80% of effective ship contracts, and the October 2026 financing raised revolver commitments to about USD 2.8 billion. If Net Yield stabilises, savings reach the margin and last-twelve-months leverage falls below the FY2025 level of 5.34x, the profile would move from stretched to adequate. If instead the annual report's revolver trigger survived the October amendment, Net Yield falls further than guided, or leverage rises above 5.51x without refinancing of the 2030 maturities, the view would weaken.

Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-29_exh_991.htm.jsonl, pages 1–3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 33–34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-K_2025-12-31_nclc-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 142; calculation K1; calculation L1; calculation S1
### Limitations

- No peer, market-price or rating-agency evidence is supplied, so labels such as adequate and stretched are judged against the issuer's own history and the filings, not against comparable cruise credits, and could shift once a peer set is added.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0); 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 39

- Forward figures rest on the parent's guidance, which covers the whole group rather than the issuer, so the 2026 earnings outlook and the leverage that follows from it are approximations; the group and issuer last-twelve-months adjusted EBITDA differ by only USD 1.0 million, which limits but does not remove the gap.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-29_exh_991.htm.jsonl, pages 2–4; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_exh_991.htm.jsonl, page 18; calculation G1; calculation P1

- The quarterly report gives no instrument-level debt table, revolver drawn balance, letters of credit or interim cash interest, so liquidity of USD 1,350.7 million is a rounded sum of cash and stated availability and interest cover is a proxy on interest expense, net.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 38

- Executed credit agreements and the October 2026 amendment are not supplied, so covenant headroom is not calculable and the revolver's contingent maturity cannot be confirmed or cleared, which restricts the refinancing and liquidity conclusions to the stated amounts.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_nclc-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, pages 41–42

- The effect of the October 2026 financing on issuer net debt, leverage and the maturity ladder is not stated, so every leverage and maturity figure here is at 30 September 2026 and may overstate the 2028 bucket and understate liquidity.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12
### Business profile and ownership

NCL Corporation is a Bermuda company that operates the Norwegian Cruise Line, Oceania Cruises and Regent Seven Seas Cruises brands from Miami, with a fleet of 33 ships at 30 September 2026 and 16 more on order, and it is wholly owned by Norwegian Cruise Line Holdings Ltd. Revenue is passenger ticket revenue, 68.0% of FY2025 revenue of USD 9,827.6 million, plus onboard and other revenue, 32.0%, and guests prepay, so bookings give visibility but also create refundable obligations. The issuer reports one segment, so brand revenue and any brand concentration are not established.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_nclc-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9; 10-K_2025-12-31_nclc-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 81; 10-K_2025-12-31_nclc-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 128; calculation Y4

The parent owns all ordinary shares, guarantees the exchangeable notes and contributed equity of USD 275,054 thousand in 2025, of which USD 144,980 thousand was cash, while the debt agreements restrict distributions to it. The parent is a holding company that depends on the issuer for cash, the issuer carries 98.66% of the group's reported debt, and about USD 15 billion of net book value of assets, 62.63% of total assets, is pledged as collateral for certain debt. The legal rank and security of the export-credit loans and exchangeable notes are not stated.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-K_2025-12-31_nclc-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 90; calculation N1; calculation P2
### Revenue, margins and cash conversion

Revenue is cyclical and discretionary, with strong summer seasonality and a third quarter that supplies 37.21% of nine-month revenue. Price is the weak variable: Occupancy was 104.2% against 104.0% while Net Yield fell, so ships stayed full while price fell, and passengers carried rose 24.42% against Passenger Cruise Days up 8.89%, which points to shorter voyages. About 45% of contract liabilities are refundable, so deposits are not a guaranteed source of cash.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-K_2025-12-31_nclc-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation Y1; calculation Y3; calculation D1

Margins are being held by cost control but not enough to offset price. Adjusted Net Cruise Cost excluding fuel per Capacity Day fell 0.66% while fuel expense rose 14.90% and payroll and related cost rose 12.46%, and operating margin fell to 15.42% from 18.13%. Ships, crew and port commitments run whatever the yield, so a fall in price passes quickly to EBITDA; the parent states that each 1% of Net Yield is worth about USD 76 million of Adjusted EBITDA over the full year.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 34–35; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_exh_991.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation K1; calculation Y1; calculation S1

Cash conversion is poor because capital spending is large and committed: last-twelve-months free cash flow was a deficit of USD 560.7 million, interest expense, net was USD 753.1 million, and cash interest paid is not stated for 2026. Discretionary room lies mainly in non-newbuild spending of about USD 0.1 billion for the rest of 2026 and in the private-destination and other growth projects inside the guided USD 1.1 billion; delivery dates have already been reset for sustainability modifications and yard availability.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 40; calculation F1; calculation I1
### Market forces in credit terms

Competition is intense and visible in price. Carnival, Royal Caribbean, MSC, Viking and Virgin Voyages compete with land-based holidays, and Net Yield fell while capacity grew, which shows rivalry rather than pricing power; entry barriers are high because ship orders total USD 19,421,174 thousand and shipyard consolidation can raise newbuild prices, so a new entrant is a smaller threat than existing capacity. Guests can cancel, with about 45% of contract liabilities refundable, and suppliers matter through shipyards, fuel, ports and third-party crew and hotel services.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_nclc-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 48–49; calculation Y1; calculation C1

Regulation and macro factors are material to credit. The EU emissions trading scheme moves to 100% of covered emissions in 2026, with USD 34.2 million of 2025 expense mostly collected from passengers, Bermuda corporate income tax of 15% applies from 2025 with an exclusion for international shipping income, the Middle East conflict is cited as pressure on revenue and fuel costs, and euro exposure runs through ship contracts and debt.

In credit terms the strengths are scale, prepaid bookings, demonstrated market access and committed export-credit funding; the weaknesses are leverage, negative free cash flow, falling yield and the 2030 maturity concentration; the opportunities are cost savings and the 2027 yield recovery that management expects; the threats are demand weakness in the Caribbean, fuel and euro moves, and a failure to refinance the 2030 maturities.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 33–34
### Outlook

Over the next 12 to 24 months the parent guides fourth-quarter 2026 Net Yield down about 6.5% and adjusted EBITDA of about USD 414 million against USD 564.0 million in the fourth quarter of 2025, which is a fall of 26.60%, with the Net Yield outlook citing a delayed Seven Seas Prestige delivery and cancelled Suez voyages, and expects Net Yield growth of 1% to 2% in 2027. On the parent's full-year guidance and debt unchanged from 30 September 2026, total debt would be 5.84x adjusted EBITDA at year-end, so leverage is more likely to rise than fall in 2026 before the 2027 recovery that management expects, and the October 2026 financing effect on debt is not established. Over three to five years deliveries continue to 2037, with non-cancelable payments of USD 3,274,155 thousand in 2030 alone, so deleveraging depends on earnings growth from new capacity, not on lower spending.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-29_exh_991.htm.jsonl, pages 1–4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 20; calculation G1; calculation Y2
### Downside scenario

The initiating condition is a further fall in Caribbean pricing as new capacity arrives and the Middle East conflict keeps Europe and Asia-Pacific demand weak. The first operational break is the booking curve, which management already describes as below its optimal range, so ships sail full at lower prices; at the parent's stated sensitivity a further 5% fall in Net Yield removes about USD 380 million of adjusted EBITDA, taking last-twelve-months adjusted EBITDA to USD 2,320.1 million, leverage to 6.42x, interest cover to 3.08x and free cash flow to a deficit of USD 940.7 million. The financing consequence is that liquidity of USD 1,350.7 million, about equal to principal due through 2027, would be drawn to fund the gap while export-credit financing still covers about 80% of ship contracts, and the 2030 maturities of USD 4,134.3 million would have to be refinanced at leverage of 6.42x. Management levers are the savings programmes, the sale or charter of older ships and the reset of delivery dates; the parent has contributed equity before but is not committed to do so. The observable triggers are adjusted EBITDA below guidance, a fourth-quarter Net Yield decline worse than the guided 6.5%, and any sign that the contingent revolver maturity applies. Management states that liquidity is sufficient for at least the next 12 months, and in the stress case resilience rests on export-credit draws and the revolver rather than on internally generated cash, so it is enough to avoid distress but not to deleverage.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 32–33; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 38; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_exh_991.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation S1; calculation Q1; calculation M1
### Overall credit view

Overall, NCL Corporation presents an adequate business profile supported by scale across three brands, prepaid bookings and demonstrated market access, but credit quality is constrained by leverage of 5.51x adjusted EBITDA, negative free cash flow and falling yields. Cash-flow durability appears weak to adequate because earnings are price-sensitive while ship payments are fixed. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on stabilising Net Yield, the unverified revolver terms and the 2030 maturities. The primary downside path is yield erosion on growing capacity that raises leverage and widens the funding gap before 2030. Further analysis would require the credit agreement and amendment, an issuer-level pro forma position after October 2026, interim cash interest and peer or market evidence. Top risk: yield erosion.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0); calculation L1; calculation S1
### Strengths and weaknesses

- Strength: scale, three brands and prepaid bookings give revenue visibility. The issuer operates 33 ships, earned revenue of USD 9,827.6 million in FY2025, filled ships to 104.2% occupancy in nine months 2026 and holds USD 3,141,976 thousand of customer deposits, which fund operations before sailing and give visibility on the next quarters, although management describes the booked position as below its optimal range. About 45% of contract liabilities are refundable, so the cushion reverses if bookings or card-processor terms change.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_nclc-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 121; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 9, 34

- Strength: market access and committed export-credit funding lower refinancing risk. The issuer placed USD 1.8 billion, USD 1.2 billion and USD 850.0 million of senior notes in 2025 and USD 950.0 million in October 2026, has about USD 10.8 billion of committed undrawn export-credit facilities and raised revolver commitments to about USD 2.8 billion, so near-term cash calls on ship deliveries are largely pre-funded and maturities have been pushed out.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 42

- Strength: the parent has supported rather than drained the issuer. Cash equity of USD 144,980 thousand in 2025, no distribution shown in the statements and restrictions on distributions in the debt agreements keep cash in the credit group, though capacity to distribute is not measured.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A)

- Strength: cost control and asset monetisation partly offset weak yield. Adjusted Net Cruise Cost excluding fuel per Capacity Day fell 0.66%, savings programmes of USD 125 million plus about USD 100 million twice are in progress, and the Sirena sale produced USD 104,995 thousand of cash proceeds, so margin and liquidity have some management levers.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 33–35; calculation K1

- Weakness: leverage is high and rising. Total debt was 5.51x last-twelve-months adjusted EBITDA against 5.34x at year-end 2025, because debt for new ships grew while adjusted EBITDA slipped, so the issuer enters its 2030 maturities with little deleveraging achieved.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation L1

- Weakness: free cash flow is negative and spending is committed. The last-twelve-months deficit of USD 560.7 million and non-cancelable ship payments of USD 19,421,174 thousand mean debt rises with deliveries and cash interest competes with capital spending for the same cash.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 20; calculation F1; calculation C1

- Weakness: yield is falling on growing capacity. Net Yield fell 3.42% in nine months and 6.51% in the third quarter, and the parent guides FY2026 adjusted EBITDA 6.64% below FY2025, so earnings are moving the wrong way while debt service and ship payments are fixed.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 34; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_exh_991.htm.jsonl, pages 2–4; calculation Y1; calculation G1

- Weakness: maturities concentrate in 2030 and the revolver term is unverified. USD 4,134.3 million, 26.68% of scheduled principal, falls due in 2030, and the annual report's contingent 17 November 2026 revolver maturity cannot be cleared without the amendment text, so refinancing risk is bunched and partly opaque.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_nclc-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 142; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 12; calculation M1

- Weakness: demand and currency exposure is concentrated. About 84% of revenue comes from U.S.-sourced guests, Europe and Asia-Pacific revenue are falling, fuel is about 48% hedged for the rest of 2026 and euro ship contracts and debt are partly unhedged, so one source market and two price shocks can move earnings together.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nclc-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 33; 10-K_2025-12-31_nclc-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 79; calculation G2
